scenarios.title: torn write
scenarios.detail: The log is cut in half through its last record, which is what a process killed mid-append leaves. Replay stops at the first record it cannot trust and keeps everything before it.

scenarios.title: flipped byte
scenarios.detail: One byte inside the last log record is inverted. The record is whole and its checksum no longer matches, so replay discards it rather than believing it.

scenarios.title: crash mid flush
scenarios.detail: A table loses the footer that would have committed it. The footer is the commit point, so the file is passed over and its records come back from the log.

scenarios.title: crash mid compaction
scenarios.detail: A real merge is killed before its footer, leaving a partial output beside its sources. The sources are still the truth, and they are all loaded again.

scenarios.title: missing footer
scenarios.detail: A committed table's footer is damaged so it no longer passes its own checksum. A footer the engine cannot verify is a footer it does not have, and it says so.

scenarios.title: expired record
scenarios.detail: A record is rewritten with a deadline that then passes. Recovery keeps it, because an expiry is a fact about the record and not damage to it, and the read path declines to return it.
